Incident_Summary: A landowner in Thika filed ELC Case 543 of 2017 alleging trespass for construction of a public road on his registered land bordering a river. Defendants alleged the road followed the riparian and road reserve boundary. Judgment delivered 10 June 2021.
Source_Name: Kenya Law Reports

Incident_Summary: The Manguo Swamp near Limuru in Kiambu County has dried up almost entirely due to encroachment, agriculture, overgrazing, and climate change. This triggered water access conflicts for residents who previously relied on the swamp.
Source_Name: Mongabay; National Museums of Kenya; Limuru Water and Sewerage Co.

Incident_Summary: Construction of a RJWSC water supply pipeline along the Thika Road corridor in Githunguri, Kiambu passed through private land parcels without fully compensating all affected owners. Several landowners physically resisted the installation.
Source_Name: NLC; RJWSC; Kiambu County

Incident_Summary: The Ondiri Swamp near Limuru, one of the two study sites for a 2011 Biodiversity journal paper on highland wetland management in Kenya, has experienced sustained encroachment and degradation, reducing its water retention function.
Source_Name: Mongabay; National Museums of Kenya; NEMA

Incident_Summary: In ELC Case E009/2023, a group of 30 interested parties supported WRA's conservation designation of Lari Swamp while 29 plaintiffs challenged it, revealing a genuine community division between those who favour conservation and those with development plans on titled land.
Source_Name: Kenya Law Reports

Incident_Summary: Encroachment on the southern Aberdare Forest in Kiambu County by squatters, small-scale farmers, and large tea estates has reduced the water tower's capacity, triggering conflicts over diminishing river flows.
Source_Name: Mongabay; KFS; NEMA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: A group of 15 downstream farmers filed a High Court petition arguing KWSC's increased Kiambu River abstraction during the 2019 drought violated their registered water allocation permits. Eventually resolved through WRMA mediation.
Source_Name: WRMA; High Court Nairobi; Kiambu County

Incident_Summary: Smallholder farmers in the Thika-Maragua border zone competed with urban Thika for water abstraction rights from the Maragua River, a tributary of the Tana River, during dry seasons.
Source_Name: WRMA; Nation Media; Tana Water Services Board

Incident_Summary: Construction of a county government water pan in Githiga area of Gatundu, Kiambu County was challenged by a private individual claiming the land as registered private property. Conflict between community water need and private land rights.
Source_Name: Kiambu County Government; NLC; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: The Baricho irrigation scheme on the Thika River conflicted with Thika town's growing municipal water demand. WRMA favoured domestic use priority. Case proceeded to Water Appeals Board in 2019 and was resolved through a seasonal allocation agreement.
Source_Name: WRMA; Water Appeals Board; Thika-Chania Water Company

Incident_Summary: Tea and smallholder farming communities along Tana River headwaters on the Kiambu-Murang'a border conflict with TAWWDA and WRMA over catchment land use restrictions that limit agricultural activity in the river's protected zone.
Source_Name: WRMA; TAWWDA; Kiambu County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A tea factory in Lari sub-county abstracted river water for tea processing at volumes that reduced domestic water availability for surrounding small farmers and households, triggering WRMA complaints.
Source_Name: WRMA; Kiambu County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Smallholder farming communities encroaching on Ndakaini (Thika) Dam's feeder streams in Kiambu County reduced catchment integrity and contributed to declining dam levels, creating a critical urban-rural water security conflict.
Source_Name: NCWSC; WRMA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Construction of the Northern Bypass highway extension through Ruiru, Kiambu County created drainage disruption conflicts as the road embankment blocked seasonal water flows.
Source_Name: KENHA; Kiambu County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Illegal sand harvesting from the Githiga River in Gatundu, Kiambu lowered the river bed, reduced the local water table, and caused bank erosion and land loss, creating conflicts between sand harvesters, adjacent farmers, and NEMA.
Source_Name: NEMA; Kiambu County; Standard Media; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Kenya Prisons Service's Kamiti Maximum Security Prison abstracting large water volumes from local boreholes in Kiambu created water access conflicts with surrounding communities experiencing water shortage.
Source_Name: WRMA; Kiambu County; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Farmers along the Sagana Road corridor in Thika built unauthorized diversion structures on seasonal rivers, reducing water flows used by downstream communities and creating conflicts arbitrated by WRMA.
Source_Name: WRMA; Tana Water Services Board; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Proliferation of unregulated private boreholes in rapidly urbanising Kinoo, Kikuyu Sub-County, Kiambu supplied water of unverified quality, creating conflicts between residents, borehole operators, and public health authorities. A 2022 cholera outbreak heightened tensions.
Source_Name: KEBS; NEMA; Kiambu County Public Health; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Rapid apartment construction along Kiambu Road from Githurai to Ruiru drove extensive borehole drilling that collectively depleted the shared aquifer, creating community water access conflicts.
Source_Name: WRMA; Mongabay; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: A squatter community of over 200 families in Kalimoni, Thika, living adjacent to the Thika River's riparian zone, faced dual eviction pressure from both a private developer claiming a title deed and the county government seeking to restore the riparian reserve.
Source_Name: NLC; ELC Thika; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: ELC Machakos dismissed Aimi Ma Lukenya's case over 4298 acres of EAPCC land on 9 October 2023. An 11-day government demolition operation followed, displacing hundreds of families. Governor Wavinya Ndeti publicly condemned the demolitions as inhumane.
Source_Name: The Star; Daily Nation; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Seasonal wetlands in the Syokimau area of Mavoko were converted to real estate developments, causing flooding and water table decline in an area experiencing rapid urbanization.
Source_Name: NEMA; Machakos County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: On 6 September 2024 bulldozers demolished structures of several families on NSSF Staff Pension Scheme land at Katani, Mavoko following a court order. Police kept vigil during the demolitions.
Source_Name: The Star

Incident_Summary: Communities practicing flood-recession agriculture on the Athi River floodplain in Kangundo contested restrictions imposed after government water management plans attempted to regulate floodplain use.
Source_Name: WRMA; NLC; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: A commercial borehole drilled for a hotel in Nzambani area of Mutomo depleted the aquifer feeding several community boreholes, triggering community protests and WRMA enforcement.
Source_Name: WRMA; Machakos County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A land cartel backed by powerful political and business figures in Mavoko blocked legitimate landowners from accessing their property. NIS briefs identified foreign financing. The Daily Nation exposed the scheme in February 2023.
Source_Name: Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: The Nol Turesh pipeline, drawing water from Mt. Kilimanjaro in Kajiado County, serves Machakos and Makueni counties. Kajiado accused Machakos of sidelining the Maasai community in water access despite the dam being in Kajiado.
Source_Name: Academic Study (Githaiga & Muchiri 2017); Journal of CMSD; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Syokimau Developers and Business Association petitioned the Machakos County Assembly seeking protection of ownership of parcels LR No. 13323/1 to 13323/124, disputed by a rival association claiming the land is public utility land.
Source_Name: Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: 54 plaintiffs filed ELC Machakos Case 227/2017 against EPZA and KMC over two large land parcels in Athi River. Court ordered plaintiffs to vacate LR No. 10281 within 90 days from October 2024.
Source_Name: Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: Inadequate piped water supply in rapidly growing Mlolongo, Machakos County created a dominant private water tanker ecosystem. Conflicts arose over tanker water pricing, borehole licensing, and impact on community groundwater.
Source_Name: WRMA; Mavoko Water; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Squatters settled on land within the Yatta Irrigation Scheme in Machakos County, competing with scheme farmers for water and land. NIA attempted multiple evictions. Court injunctions were sought by squatters.
Source_Name: NIA; Machakos ELC; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A tractor was observed digging trenches on a disputed 10-acre parcel near Daystar University in Athi River on 10 December 2023. Residents accused rogue police of complicity in land grabbing.
Source_Name: Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Siltation of Mwania Dam in Machakos County caused by upstream agricultural activity reduced the dam's water storage, triggering conflict between dam users and upstream farming communities.
Source_Name: Machakos County Water Department; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: EAPCC issued a public buyer beware warning in 2016 that buyers should not purchase land within its registered 4,298-acre parcel. Despite the warning, thousands continued to buy from brokers, leading to the 2023 demolitions.
Source_Name: The Star

Incident_Summary: Seasonal flash floods along the Athi River in April 2023 affected informal settlements that had encroached on the river floodplain near Athi River town, prompting renewed calls for riparian enforcement in Machakos.
Source_Name: Machakos County; NDMU; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Effluent from the Athi River Industrial Zone contaminated the Athi River, destroying irrigation water quality for downstream Mavoko farmers and creating land use conflicts near the contaminated river corridor.
Source_Name: NEMA; WRMA; GRIN Study; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: The Ruiru II Dam project and associated water transfer infrastructure in the Kiambu-Machakos boundary zone generated land acquisition and water rights conflicts with communities in the catchment area.
Source_Name: Huduma Global; NLC; AWWDA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Siltation of community water pans on the Yatta Plateau in Machakos due to upstream land clearing and poor catchment management reduced water storage capacity, creating conflicts over water availability and desilting responsibility.
Source_Name: NWCPC; Machakos County; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Construction of the Thwake Multipurpose Dam on the Thwake River in Makueni County impacts Machakos County communities through catchment area land use restrictions and water allocation questions.
Source_Name: Huduma Global; NLC; AWWDA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: A private developer in Kinanie, Machakos County destroyed an irrigation furrow serving 45 smallholder farming families by erecting a perimeter wall across its path. County mediation led to a culvert being installed, only partially resolving the problem.
Source_Name: Machakos County Irrigation Department; Sub-County Administration

Incident_Summary: Farming in the upper Tana catchment flowing into Masinga Dam reduced water quality and quantity for Kenya's largest hydroelectric dam, creating a systemic land-water conflict between energy needs and agricultural livelihoods.
Source_Name: KenGen; WRMA; NLC; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: EPZA industrial tenants in the Athi River Export Processing Zone required large water volumes, competing with Mavoko Water and Sewerage Company's ability to meet growing residential demand.
Source_Name: WRMA; EPZA; Mavoko Water and Sewerage Company; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Communities living near the Kiambere Reservoir on the upper Tana River in the Machakos-Kitui boundary contested displacement and inadequate compensation from the reservoir's expansion and management restrictions.
Source_Name: KenGen; NLC; WRMA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Land sold by British American Tobacco (BAT) in the early 1990s in Athi River became subject to cartel activity, with legitimate purchasers unable to access their properties due to cartel-hired gangs.
Source_Name: Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: Unsustainable sand harvesting from the Athi River bed in Machakos County has lowered the riverbed, reduced groundwater availability, and undermined riverbank structures, creating conflicts with downstream water users and farmers.
Source_Name: NEMA; WRMA; GRIN Academic Study; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Unregulated and licensed sand harvesting from the Athi River bed and banks in Machakos County destabilized banks, caused river course migration, and generated conflicts with riparian landowners.
Source_Name: NEMA; WRMA; Water Action Hub; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A joint community water project serving Kambu and Kola villages in Machakos County became a source of intra-community conflict over management, cost-sharing, and access scheduling.
Source_Name: Machakos County Water Department; Area Chief Records

Incident_Summary: Illegal sand harvesting pits left open along Mwala's seasonal rivers became waterlogged during rains, providing breeding grounds for malaria mosquitoes, creating a public health land-water conflict.
Source_Name: Machakos County Public Health; County Assembly Records; NEMA

Incident_Summary: A 7-acre wetland in Kileleshwa known as Dik Dik Gardens was subdivided into 17 private titled plots, threatening its function as primary water source for Kirichwa Ndogo River. WRA gazetted it as a Conservation Area in October 2021 under Legal Notice 206/2021.
Source_Name: Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 187 - Legal Notice 206/2021

Incident_Summary: The High Court ruled that forced evictions and demolitions in Mathare and Gwa Kairu slums following the April 2024 floods were illegal and unconstitutional. Government ordered to compensate displaced residents.
Source_Name: Standard Media; Citizen Digital

Incident_Summary: Governor Sakaja announced active clearance of Kirichwa Kubwa River corridor encroachments in Kilimani in 2025, with the governor directly quoted warning planners that no property owner on riparian land would be exempted.
Source_Name: Eastleigh Voice

Incident_Summary: Mukuru Kwa Ruben residents were forcibly evicted following April 2024 floods. High Court declared evictions unconstitutional and ordered compensation. Residents had lived there for decades on privately owned land.
Source_Name: Standard Media; SDI; Akiba Mashinani Trust; HIC-GS

Incident_Summary: 29 private landowners on Kiambu/Lari parcels challenged WRA's conservation designation of Lari Swamp - a 244.66-hectare wetland feeding Ruiru River - in ELC Case E009 of 2023. WRA countered that the swamp is a critical water source for greater Nairobi environs.
Source_Name: Kenya Law Reports

Incident_Summary: Kiamaiko residents forcibly evicted after April 2024 floods. High Court ruled evictions illegal. Justice Mogeni ordered government compensation for loss of property. Residents left homeless without alternative shelter.
Source_Name: Standard Media; Hakijamii; Citizen Digital

Incident_Summary: November 2021 violent forced eviction at Mukuru Kwa Njenga along Catherine Ndereba Road displaced hundreds. NMS arrived without warning, demolishing homes beyond the designated road corridor. 40,000 residents at risk.
Source_Name: HIC-GS; Amnesty Kenya; The Guardian; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A Westlands family was evicted from their home of 46 years after a rival claimant obtained an ELC eviction order. The family lacked formal title despite decades of occupation. Documented in TI Kenya's 2025 housing rights review.
Source_Name: Standard Media; Tuko.co.ke; TI-Kenya Housing Rights Review (2025)

Incident_Summary: The Nubian community of Kibera challenged eviction by KURA for the Southern Bypass road construction, claiming Kibera is their ancestral land. High Court temporarily barred KURA from eviction. Court heard on 18 October (year approximate).
Source_Name: HLRN; High Court Kenya; The Conversation; Kenya Urban Roads Authority

Incident_Summary: Following the April 2024 floods, Cabinet issued orders requiring all residents of risk-prone and riparian areas to move out. Amnesty Kenya issued a solidarity statement condemning the evictions of informal settlement residents.
Source_Name: TI Kenya; Amnesty Kenya; Government of Kenya

Incident_Summary: Residents of Deep Sea informal settlement in Westlands have faced continuous threat of eviction due to tenure insecurity. Hakijamii documented the settlement as part of the systemic crisis of land-water conflict in Nairobi informal settlements.
Source_Name: Hakijamii

Incident_Summary: Commercial activities in Eastleigh discharged untreated wastewater and solid waste into the Mathare River corridor, causing land devaluation, flooding, and public health conflicts in Mathare Valley downstream.
Source_Name: NEMA; Nation Media; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A developer in the Karen Hardy area sought to drain and develop a wetland connected to the Ngong River system. Karen residents and NEMA challenged the development on environmental grounds.
Source_Name: NEMA; NLC; Standard Media; Karen Residents Association

Incident_Summary: Construction of the Southern Bypass through Kibera altered drainage patterns, causing downstream flooding in sections of the slum previously unaffected. Compensation for affected residents remained disputed.
Source_Name: KENHA; Kenya Red Cross; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: On 24 April 2024 the Mathare River burst its banks due to heavy rainfall, killing dozens of residents. The disaster triggered the national riparian eviction policy and the KSh 50 billion Nairobi River Regeneration Programme.
Source_Name: Standard Media; Nation Media; Kenya Red Cross

Incident_Summary: The Nairobi River between Ngara and Eastleigh has been completely encroached by informal and formal structures, with the river reduced to a polluted drain. Disputes arise over eviction, environmental enforcement, and water quality.
Source_Name: NEMA; Daily Nation; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Waithaka and Kawangware informal settlements, identified in academic studies as having relatively more secure land tenure than other Nairobi slums, nonetheless faced riparian encroachment conflicts particularly along the Nairobi River tributaries.
Source_Name: World Bank/IGAD Academic Study; NLC; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Factories in the Nairobi Industrial Area discharge effluent into drainage channels flowing through Mukuru kwa Njenga, contaminating water sources used by informal settlement residents and adding to flooding risk.
Source_Name: NEMA; Kenya Human Rights Commission; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Residents of Mukuru Sinai faced eviction by Kenya Pipeline Company which planned to expand its petroleum pipeline. Residents had built on both sides of the pipeline without legal title, complicating compensation and relocation.
Source_Name: SDI; Pamoja Trust; Muungano wa Wanavijiji

Incident_Summary: Blocked storm drainage channels in the Nairobi CBD regularly flood Tom Mboya Street and adjacent commercial streets due to illegal solid waste dumping into drainage inlets by vendors, creating recurring land-water use conflicts.
Source_Name: KURA; NEMA; Nation Media; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Rapid high-density development in South C overwhelmed the area's sewage infrastructure, causing chronic sewage backups into residential properties and creating land-water use conflicts between residents and NCWSC.
Source_Name: NCWSC; Standard Media; South C Residents Association

Incident_Summary: Residents of Mathare paid exploitative prices to private water vendors due to inadequate piped water supply, creating a water access conflict that intersects with the land tenure insecurity of the informal settlement.
Source_Name: SDI; NCWSC; Nation Media; Hakijamii

Incident_Summary: The Dandora dumpsite, one of the largest open landfills in East Africa, leaches toxic fluids into the Nairobi River and adjacent aquifers, contaminating water for communities in Ruai, Dandora, and downstream Machakos.
Source_Name: NEMA; Community Health Reports; Nation Media; Academic Literature

Incident_Summary: Residents of Korogocho settled on land that was later discovered to be a reserved road reserve and drainage corridor. Eviction attempts by KENHA were resisted by residents backed by civil society groups.
Source_Name: KENHA; Nation Media; Civil Society Documentation

Incident_Summary: The Pangani Slum Upgrading Project in Mathare North displaced residents to make way for formal housing, but water infrastructure conflicts arose between the developer, displaced residents, and the county.
Source_Name: Nation Media; Standard Media; Amnesty International

Incident_Summary: Gikomba Market, Africa's largest second-hand clothes market, has encroached on the Nairobi River bank near Ngara Bridge, with market waste and stalls directly on the riparian zone, contributing to chronic flooding and river pollution.
Source_Name: Nairobi River Cleanup Partnership; NEMA; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Inadequate NCWSC supply to dense Pumwani and Eastleigh areas created a water vending ecosystem with conflicts over metering, pricing, and landlords using water shutoffs as leverage in rent disputes.
Source_Name: NCWSC; Nation Media; Nairobi Human Rights Commission

Incident_Summary: Several River Road buildings in central Nairobi were found to be built over underground tributaries of the Nairobi River, causing structural subsidence. NLC investigated title deeds while NEMA raised environmental concerns.
Source_Name: Nation Media; NLC; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Collapse of the NCWSC sewer main in Riruta Satellite caused raw sewage to flow into the Nairobi River's upper reaches and onto adjacent residential land, creating health and property conflicts.
Source_Name: NCWSC; NEMA; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: The northern branch of the Nairobi River flowing through Kasarani and Roysambu has been progressively encroached by residential and commercial developments over two decades, contributing to flooding and water quality conflicts.
Source_Name: Daily Nation; NEMA; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Severe water shortage in Pangani triggered conflicts between landlords drilling unlicensed boreholes for apartment buildings and NCWSC, which reported reduced flows partially attributable to private borehole competition drawing down the shared aquifer.
Source_Name: WRMA; NCWSC; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: The Ngong Road Forest on Nairobi's southwestern edge faced excision attempts by politically connected land grabbers. The forest serves as a critical water catchment for Nairobi's southern drainage. Civil society interventions blocked most excisions.
Source_Name: KFS; NLC; NEMA; Nation Media; Civil Society

Incident_Summary: Prior to the 2021 WRA gazettement of Dik Dik Gardens as a Conservation Area, a multi-year conflict between private title holders of the subdivided wetland and public interest institutions including WRA, NEMA, and the Nairobi County Environmental Department remained unresolved.
Source_Name: Kenya Gazette LN 206/2021

Incident_Summary: Sand and gravel harvesting from rivers in the Utawala-Joska area on the Nairobi-Machakos border destabilized riverbanks, caused flooding, and created legal land boundary conflicts.
Source_Name: NEMA; Nairobi County; Machakos County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: A developer in Umoja-Mwiki constructed a warehouse that partially blocked a KENHA storm drainage easement, causing upstream flooding of residential properties during every rain season since 2020. Legal proceedings were ongoing as of 2024.
Source_Name: KENHA; Standard Media; Nairobi County

Incident_Summary: Industrial Area firms along the Nairobi River south bank have occupied the river's riparian reserve for storage yards, parking, and effluent channels, creating a systemic land-water conflict with regulatory authorities.
Source_Name: NEMA; Daily Nation; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Operation Maliza Uhalifu launched 13 February 2023 in North Rift following a 77% increase in pastoralist militia violence in Q1 2023 vs late 2022. By Q4 2023, ACLED recorded over 90% fall in militia events in Turkana County.
Source_Name: ACLED; ReliefWeb; The New Humanitarian; ICG

Incident_Summary: Kapedo on the Baringo-Turkana border has been the site of intense inter-communal conflict primarily driven by competition over water points and pasture. ICG documented 239 deaths across northern Rift Valley since May 2021.
Source_Name: ICG; New Lines Magazine; New Humanitarian; ACLED

Incident_Summary: Pokot militia from Tiaty constituency in Baringo County were identified by ICG and ACLED as the most active violent actor in the North Rift in 2022-2023, conducting raids on Turkana communities over water and pasture.
Source_Name: ACLED; ICG; New Humanitarian; Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: Latest cycle of North Rift violence erupted May 2021 at Laikipia-Baringo border and spread to Baringo-Turkana boundary. At least 239 people were killed across the region by mid-2023. In Q1 2022 alone, Baringo fatalities more than doubled compared to all of 2021.
Source_Name: International Crisis Group; ACLED; Journal of Eastern African Studies; The New Humanitarian

Incident_Summary: In 2023-2024, an Interpeace peace dialogue in Kapedo observed by The New Humanitarian revealed continued deep distrust between Pokot and Turkana communities, with disarmament remaining a key sticking point despite agreement on ceasing attacks.
Source_Name: The New Humanitarian

Incident_Summary: A group of approximately 50 armed Pokot militia ambushed a civilian police truck near Lomelo village in Turkana North, 25 miles northwest of Kapedo. A 13-year-old boy was among those on the truck.
Source_Name: New Lines Magazine

Incident_Summary: On March 17, 2023, RDU police responded to a bandit attack at Yatya in Baringo North on the Turkana border. The attack exemplified the ongoing armed conflict over pastoral water and pasture resources.
Source_Name: Daily Nation

Incident_Summary: Todonyang community elder Muchu Lomorukai Kerio documented the severe impact of climate change on water and pasture in Todonyang, Lake Turkana, and resulting community disputes as pastoralists shift to fishing - itself creating new conflicts.
Source_Name: Water, Peace and Security Partnership - International Alert

Incident_Summary: The Kenyan government launched a major security operation in the North Rift on February 13, 2023, targeting pastoralist militias. Turkana Governor condemned army use of artillery on civilian areas in March 2023.
Source_Name: ACLED; ICG; Daily Nation; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: About 700 IDP households at Canaan Camp in Kanamkemer, Lodwar were provided water kiosks by an aid agency. After handover to LOWASCO, governance failures led to water access conflicts.
Source_Name: International Alert / Water Peace and Security

Incident_Summary: In Kibish, Turkana North, access to generator-powered borehole water was conditioned on payment. Those unable to pay were excluded from watering their livestock, and disputes arose over access scheduling and payment collection.
Source_Name: International Alert / Water Peace and Security

Incident_Summary: The 2022-2023 drought -” the worst in 40 years, with four consecutive failed rainy seasons -” left over 4 million Kenyans in need of emergency water assistance, intensifying land-water conflicts across Turkana County.
Source_Name: Huduma Global; ICG; WFP; ACLED

Incident_Summary: Water release decisions from the Turkwel Gorge Hydroelectric Dam on the Turkwel River in Turkana County created conflicts with downstream pastoralist communities dependent on controlled river flow for water and grazing.
Source_Name: WRMA; KenGen; Turkana County; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Turkana North fishing communities conflict with KWS and Sibiloi National Park authorities over access to fish breeding grounds on Lake Turkana's protected islands, crucial for fish stocks.
Source_Name: Water Peace and Security - International Alert

Incident_Summary: Counter-intuitive pattern documented by SCCRR and academic researchers: violent raids between Turkana and Pokot increase during rainy seasons as communities compete over newly discovered aquifer recharge points.
Source_Name: SCCRR; ACCORD; Academic Literature

Incident_Summary: Introduction of Regional Rangeland Management Committees to regulate grazing access in Turkana conflicts with traditional communal rangeland practices and creates disputes over who controls migration routes and water-adjacent grazing areas.
Source_Name: International Alert / Water Peace and Security

Incident_Summary: An organised water cartel known locally as nakana illegally connected pipes to Kalokol town's main water line, diverting water for private sale and depriving legitimate users.
Source_Name: International Alert / Water Peace and Security

Incident_Summary: Turkana host community members reported exclusion from UNHCR-managed boreholes in Kakuma, triggering community protests and mediation by UNHCR and Turkana County Government.
Source_Name: UNHCR Kenya; Turkana County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: Five consecutive failed rainy seasons (2020-early 2023) - the longest dry spell in at least 40 years - drove mass livestock mortality, land abandonment, and forced migration in Turkana and adjacent counties, intensifying all land and water conflicts.
Source_Name: International Crisis Group; Kenya Meteorological Department; Climate Hazards Center

Incident_Summary: Tullow Oil's drilling at Ngamia 1 oil block in Lokichar Basin from June 2012 required water for drilling operations. Community conflicts arose over use of local water sources and perceived exclusion from economic benefits.
Source_Name: Frontiers Environmental Science; Business Daily Africa; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: International Alert's WPS report documented that oil firms' water requirements in Turkana may fuel further conflict, as drilling and hydraulic fracturing compete with pastoral communities for the same aquifers.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; Business Daily Africa

Incident_Summary: Deforestation for firewood around Kakuma Refugee Camp by the large refugee population led to land degradation, loss of vegetation cover for water catchment, and tension with host community members.
Source_Name: UNHCR Kenya; Kenya Forest Service; Turkana County

Incident_Summary: In July-September 2022, following the driest rainy season on record, armed Pokot groups attacked smallholding communities along the Baringo-Turkana boundary, displacing hundreds of households.
Source_Name: Journal of Eastern African Studies; ICG; The New Humanitarian

Incident_Summary: Two Turkana sub-clan groups competed violently over control of the Nadoto water point in Loima Sub-County, Turkana County, during an extreme dry season in 2016.
Source_Name: SCCRR Conflict Incidence Reports; Loima Sub-County Administration

Incident_Summary: The November 2012 Baragoi Massacre -” in which Samburu warriors killed over 40 Kenyan police officers responding to a Turkana-Samburu cattle raid -” marked a peak of violence in the contested water-pasture corridor.
Source_Name: ACCORD; Nation Media; Kenya Human Rights Commission

Incident_Summary: The Karamoja Cluster cross-border conflict zone spans Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan, and Ethiopia, involving multiple ethnic pastoralist groups competing over water points, grazing land, and livestock. Defined as one of the most persistent conflict zones in East Africa.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; ACCORD

Incident_Summary: The LAPSSET corridor passes through Turkana County requiring large land acquisitions. Pastoralists whose traditional routes and water access points fall within the corridor have experienced conflicts over compensation and access restriction.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; NLC; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Ambiguity in the boundary between Turkana and Marsabit counties in the Lake Turkana northern region created conflicts between fishing communities from each county over fishing territories on the lake.
Source_Name: Kenya Fisheries Service; County Boundary Commission; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Despite chronic drought, Turkana County has experienced erratic intense flooding events since 2021, creating conflicts over floodwater access for agriculture versus the displacement and property destruction floods cause.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; ACLED; Kenya Red Cross

Incident_Summary: National and county government ASAL water security programmes in Turkana encountered land disputes when selecting sites for water pans, boreholes, and sand dams, with communities contesting ownership of proposed sites.
Source_Name: NDMA; Turkana County; WaterAid; Nation Media

Incident_Summary: Flash flooding of the Kerio River in October 2019 displaced thousands of Turkana pastoralists camped on the floodplain, destroying homes and livestock camps and triggering competition for remaining dry land.
Source_Name: Kenya Red Cross; NDMA; Turkana County

Incident_Summary: Women in Turkana County, who bear primary responsibility for fetching household water, face disproportionate burdens and specific conflicts when water points are controlled by men or women are excluded from water user association decision-making.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; Turkana Women Peace Caucus

Incident_Summary: Dassanach community members from Ethiopia regularly cross into Kibish Sub-County in Turkana North pursuing water and grazing, creating cyclical violent conflicts with Turkana residents.
Source_Name: Wikipedia; Frontiers Environmental Science; WPS International Alert

Incident_Summary: Agricultural schemes established for Kalobeyei Settlement refugees along the Turkwel River created conflicts with Turkana host community members who felt their traditional Turkwel River water access and farmland was being allocated to refugees.
Source_Name: UNHCR Kenya; Turkana County; Standard Media

Incident_Summary: LOWASCO's water kiosk management in Lodwar has been characterised by inconsistent pricing, service interruptions, and governance failures, creating conflicts between kiosk operators, LOWASCO, and residents.
Source_Name: International Alert / WPS; Turkana County Government

Incident_Summary: The retreat of Lake Turkana exposed previously submerged land near Lothagam, creating new land claims and conflicts between the Turkana County Government, local communities, and heritage site management.
Source_Name: Turkana County; Kenya National Museums; Nation Media
